prediction.likelyOutcome: Lagoon should win summary judgment on the $364,212 unpaid-rent claim now; the frustration-of-purpose defense is weak given Landmark's own post-reopening business decisions. The $1,444,258 accelerated/future-rent claim is unlikely to be fully resolved on this early summary-judgment motion because of a genuine, record-supported mitigation dispute (Lagoon's redevelopment of the property) and because discovery (including Abdul's deposition) has not closed; expect that portion to be denied or continued, with Lagoon still favored to recover a substantial share of it at trial after the factual mitigation issues are resolved, subject to the $1,808,470 ceiling stated in its own complaint.

issues.label: Liquidated Damages Clause as Unenforceable Penalty

outcome.description: The district court granted Lagoon summary judgment in June 2022, held the liquidated-damages clause enforceable so that no mitigation was required, and (after Lagoon waived attorney fees) entered judgment for $1,808,470 plus costs. The Minnesota Court of Appeals reversed on December 11, 2023, holding the liquidated-damages clause unenforceable because actual damages were capable of estimation and the clause ignored the duty to mitigate, and remanded for further proceedings on actual damages and mitigation.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed (liquidated-damages clause unenforceable) and remanded; no final figure yet.
